 Jim Duggan Recalls Getting Busted Open By Andre The Giant During In-Ring Segment
 Jeremy Thomas --> 
 November 18, 2026 | Posted by Jeremy Thomas 
 Image Credit: WWE 
 Share on twitter 
 Share on facebook 
 Tweet 
 Hacksaw Jim Duggan recently looked back at his rivalry with Andre the Giant and getting busted open during an in-ring segment. Duggan spoke with Sporf for a new interview and recounted the encounter on the April 2, 1988 episode of WWE Superstars where he knocked Andre out.
 Duggen noted that when Andre went to grab him during the segment, the giant’s thumb busted open his lip. You can see the highlights below:
 On the WWE Superstars Segment:
 “If there was a giant in our business, Yokozuna, Umaga, The Big Show, Andre the Giant, it was ‘Duggan, get your 2×4’; I had to wrestle every giant there was. I ran down; I had my chin on Andre’s belly, I’m looking up at him like, ‘I’m not afraid of you’. He went to grab me, and his thumb hit my lip, and my lip fell down, and blood came pouring down my chest. It actually worked out great, everyone was like, ‘Where did the blood come from’? He beat me up with his thumb. WWF went off the air with me standing over Andre the Giant, covered in blood.”
 On His Pre-WWF Feud With Andre:
 “I broke into wrestling in Texas with Fritz Von Erich, but I went up to New York for the WWF. After wrestling Hulk Hogan and Sergeant Slaughter, Vince McMahon Sr. called me into his office, and he was like, ‘Kid, you might have a future, but come up with something better than ‘Big Jim’ and get rid of that gold bath robe; we’re going to send you out to learn how to wrestle. We’re going to send you to Hawaii.’ I was a young guy, and they flew me to Hawaii, where I worked for ‘High Chief’ Peter Maivia. Of course, I’m young, and I’m wrestling all these grown men. My good friend, Haku (Meng), was over there, and we were making about $40 per week. The Chinese restaurant banned us from the all-you-can-eat buffet.
 “Anyway, they put me under a mask and called me, ‘The Convict’. Andre, on his way back from Japan, stopped in Hawaii, and he was the man who tore my mask off. Of course, everybody was like, ‘Who’s this guy’? But the bottom line is that I formed a great relationship with Andre as a young man. Years later, when I came into the WWF, I’m working with Andre; he allows me to knock him out with my 2×4. That elevated me from a mid-card guy to a main event guy. If Andre didn’t want to do that, he would’ve eaten my 2×4.”
 On Working With Andre On Live Events:
 “Once in a while, when he would beat me on the house shows, he would put his feet on the ropes. For a wrestler, that’s huge, because it gives me an out: ‘You wouldn’t have beaten me if you didn’t put your feet on the ropes; you had to cheat to beat me’. I had a great relationship with the big man. It was a hard life for him. Nowadays, there are a lot of big people, but back then at 7ft4 and 500lbs, it was tough. I was lucky to have what I had with him.”
